t: 259 unique candidate core genes were identified by filtering for disease odds ratio above median, p<0.05, and mapping to at least 20% of cases in the Refinement dataset; pathway enrichment implicated nervous system development, neural signaling, immune response, cellular stress response and calcium signaling.

Hypothesis-driven functional characterization showed that over 50% of candidate core genes were linked to energy metabolism, followed by neurological processes (13.1%), inflammation/autoimmunity (10%), mitochondrial dysfunction (9.7%), and innate immunity (5.8%).

TLR3, an innate immune receptor for viral double-stranded RNA already targeted by an ME clinical trial drug, showed a novel genetic association with ME (odds ratio 1.20, p=10-4), present in a 24.1% patient subgroup.

Rintatolimod, a synthetic TLR3 agonist, has shown statistically significant improvement in primary (exercise tolerance) and some secondary endpoints in placebo-controlled Phase II/III ME clinical trials, but remains experimental with limited compassionate access in the US.

PDE4B, encoding phosphodiesterase 4B which hydrolyzes cAMP, showed a novel genetic link to ME across 44 disease signatures (OR 1.05-1.78, minimum p=1x10-12), present in around 70% of patients in both analyses, and is proposed to be modulated by apremilast.

Apremilast, an approved PDE4 inhibitor for psoriasis, is proposed as a repurposing candidate for a PDE4B-associated ME patient subgroup, and unpublished results suggest possible efficacy in a subgroup of long COVID patients too.

Large-scale phenotype association analysis linking gene-defined patient subgroups to self-reported symptoms/comorbidities did not identify associations passing FDR correction, though exploratory top-ranked gene-phenotype pairs were noted.

The count of double-refined disease signatures (excluding 6p22.1) was significantly correlated with ME case status in an independent Test dataset, with an OR of 1.23 per standard deviation increase after controlling for sex and 10 genetic PCs.
Individuals in the top decile of signature count score had 1.64-fold higher odds of ME than those in the bottom decile, and top 5% vs bottom 5% had 1.89-fold higher odds.
The double-refined ME signatures mapped to 13 of the 32 Tier 1/2 genes identified by the DecodeME GWAS, including genes located in 6 of the 8 GWAS-significant loci.

102 of the 235 (43%) previously identified long COVID genes mapped to the double-refined ME signatures, including 76 of 180 (42%) genes that had reproduced in an independent All of Us long COVID cohort, representing significant enrichment.

A length-matched permutation test confirmed significant enrichment (p<0.017) of long COVID gene overlap with ME genes across all three gene-length bins, ruling out gene-length bias as an explanation for the overlap.

MAPK9, NLGN1, and PTPRD were among the top 20 highest-ranked ME genes in the machine learning model and were also associated with Fatigue Dominant long COVID, a significantly greater overlap than expected by chance.

Top-ranked SNPs in the ML model for ME were significantly enriched among genes previously associated with Severe and Fatigue Dominant long COVID phenotypes, more so than for genes associated with endometriosis or coronary artery disease.

Six genes among the 259 candidate core genes (CSMD1, CYB5RL, MRPL37, PAX5, SRGAP1, RAP1GAP2) were also previously reported in disease signatures from an earlier, fully disjoint combinatorial analysis of a UK Biobank ME cohort, providing independent replication.

Several core candidate genes (TLR3, CD8B, CD22, PSMB9) have established roles in immune signaling and inflammation, aligning with known immune dysregulation and aberrant cytokine profiles in ME, including CD8+ T-cell exhaustion and immunoproteasome activity (PSMB9).

Metabolism-related core candidate genes PKM, IGF1R, TBC1D5, and ABCA1 were identified, consistent with impaired energy metabolism and mitochondrial dysfunction implicated in ME pathophysiology; PKM (PKM2) is mechanistically linked to IGF1R signaling and inflammasome activation.
SNP combinations underlying the double-refined signatures showed a female-to-male ratio closely aligned with the overall cohort sex ratio, suggesting the signatures are not sex-biased.
A single CpG site (cg19803194) within the PTPRN2 gene body showed significant DNA hypomethylation in ME patients compared to healthy controls, surviving Bonferroni correction and BACON adjustment.
ME patients with cg19803194 hypomethylation had a significantly longer illness duration (approximately five years longer) than ME patients with normal methylation at that site.
Hypomethylation at cg19803194 was associated in both sexes with cognitive impairments (difficulty expressing thoughts and understanding concepts), commonly termed 'brain fog'.
DNA methylation at cg19803194 was inversely correlated with severity of breathing difficulties on the DSQ, but only in male ME patients.

Multivariable regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI, illness duration, batch, and salivary cell-type fractions confirmed the inverse association between cg19803194 methylation and respiratory severity as a significant male-specific phenotype.
ME patients with cg19803194 hypomethylation had reduced plasma miR-153-3p levels compared to ME patients with normal methylation.
Circulating miR-153-3p levels were significantly associated with objective delayed memory recognition performance in a cognitively-tested subset of ME patients.
Circulating PHB2 levels showed a significant positive correlation with circulating miR-153-3p levels specifically in female ME patients.
Circulating PHB2 levels were globally higher in ME patients than healthy controls, with this elevation primarily driven by female ME patients.
A ribonucleoproteomic analysis found that intracellular PHB2 physically interacts with the stem-loop of immature miR-153-3p (pre-miR-153-2), described as unpublished data.
In HEK-293T dual-luciferase assays, PHB2 overexpression significantly increased the global Fluc/Rluc reporter ratio by 1.5-fold, indicating reduced miR-153-3p maturation/activity.
Overexpression of Argonaute 2 (Ago2), used as a positive control, reduced the global Fluc/Rluc luciferase ratio by 1.7-fold, confirming assay specificity for miR-153-3p activity.

PHB2 overexpression caused a 1.5-fold decrease in mature miR-153-3p levels by RT-qPCR, while pri-miR-153-2 and pre-miR-153-2 levels remained unchanged, indicating a post-transcriptional cytoplasmic block in maturation rather than a transcriptional effect.
Subcellular fractionation and immunoblotting showed transfected FLAG-PHB2 predominantly localizes to the cytoplasmic fraction of HEK-293T cells.

Among ME patients stratified by both cg19803194 methylation status and sex, female patients in the hypomethylation subgroup showed significantly elevated plasma PHB2 compared to male hypomethylation patients, suggesting a compensatory sex-specific pattern.
ME patients showed markedly worse physical and mental health scores and higher fatigue and symptom severity across all DSQ domains compared to healthy controls on SF-36, MFI-20, and DSQ.
No significant correlation was found between illness duration and DNA hypomethylation levels at cg19803194, suggesting the epigenetic change is not simply proportional to disease duration.

Of seven CpG sites initially showing differential methylation (Δβ≥0.13) between ME and controls, only cg19803194 (PTPRN2) survived Bonferroni correction; six other sites (including those annotated to PLEKHA4, HLA-DPB2, and intergenic regions) did not reach genome-wide significance.
Sleep-deprivation-induced CFS model mice showed a marked reduction in liver index compared with controls, which was restored to near-normal levels by EBN treatment.

In the open-field test, total distance traveled was significantly reduced in the CFS model group compared with controls, indicating reduced exploratory drive, and this was restored dose-dependently by EBN.

The Model group spent significantly less time in the center zone of the open field than controls, indicating increased anxiety-like behavior, and EBN-H treatment increased center time 5.8-fold relative to the Model group.

The CFS model group displayed significantly reduced Y-maze spontaneous alternation accuracy versus controls, reflecting working memory decline, which EBN-H treatment restored to near-normal (99% of control) levels.
Forced running duration and grip strength were significantly reduced in the CFS model group relative to controls, and EBN-H treatment markedly improved motor performance.
HE staining revealed reduced TA muscle cross-sectional area in the Model group, which was largely restored (to 98% of control) by high-dose EBN treatment.
Golgi staining showed markedly reduced synaptic cristae density in the prefrontal cortex of CFS model mice, which EBN-H treatment increased 3.3-fold relative to the Model group.

HE staining showed extensive neuronal necrosis and swelling in the prefrontal cortex of the CFS model group compared with structurally normal neurons in controls; the highest EBN dose produced the most pronounced therapeutic benefit.
Serum cortisol was significantly elevated in the sleep-deprivation CFS model group compared with controls, and was decreased in the high-dose EBN group.
Serum serotonin (5-HT) levels were significantly reduced in the CFS model group, and EBN treatment significantly improved 5-HT levels.
Serum IL-6 was significantly upregulated in the sleep-deprivation CFS model group and was reduced by EBN treatment in a dose-dependent manner.
Serum IL-1β was significantly upregulated in the CFS model group and reduced by EBN treatment in a dose-dependent manner.
Serum TNF-α was significantly upregulated in the CFS model group and reduced by EBN treatment in a dose-dependent manner.

Untargeted serum metabolomics identified the dipeptide Val-Trp as significantly and dose-dependently upregulated in EBN-treated CFS model mice, increasing 38% in the high-dose EBN group compared with the model group.
In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia, NO levels were significantly elevated compared with control, and Val-Trp treatment reduced NO content by 57% relative to the LPS group, close to control levels.

Phosphorylated NF-κB p65 expression was strongly increased in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia (model) but suppressed following Val-Trp treatment, indicating Val-Trp reduces neuroinflammation by inhibiting NF-κB activation.
Expression of iNOS, a canonical M1-like microglial phenotype marker, was significantly elevated in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia (model) but reduced after Val-Trp administration.

At the vertex level, thalamic-seeded functional connectivity at the normative negative peak (left lateral occipital cortex) did not differ significantly between CFS patients and healthy controls, but was significantly anticorrelated with fatigue severity in CFS patients.

When the negative peak vertex was expanded to a 6 mm sphere, CFS patients showed significantly lower thalamic-seeded FC than healthy controls, and FC remained significantly anticorrelated with fatigue severity.
At the normative positive peak (right cingulate gyrus), thalamic-seeded FC differed significantly between CFS patients and healthy controls but was not associated with fatigue severity.
When the positive peak vertex was expanded to a sphere, the group difference between CFS and HC remained significant and stronger, but FC remained uncorrelated with fatigue severity.

In 35 CFS patients who completed one month of Tai Chi exercise, exercise-induced increases in FC within the cortical mask targeting the negative site (left lateral occipital cortex) were significantly anticorrelated with reductions in fatigue severity.
No significant relationship was observed between exercise-induced FC changes and fatigue severity changes when targeting the positive site (right cingulate gyrus) simulation mask.

Individual-level analysis of thalamic-seeded FC peaks showed substantial spatial variability across 100 CFS patients and 100 HC, with an overlap rate of less than 8% among participants even after spatial expansion.

In individual analysis, the negative FC vertex showed a significant group difference between CFS and HC and was significantly anticorrelated with fatigue severity, but this correlation was lost when the vertex was expanded to a 6mm sphere.

In individual analysis, the positive FC vertex showed a significant group difference between CFS and HC but no correlation with fatigue severity at vertex level, whereas at sphere level both the group difference and the correlation became significant.

Site stimulation simulation using individually-derived negative and positive FC peaks showed no significant relationship between exercise-induced FC changes and fatigue severity changes for either site.

Normative analysis identified a consistent left lateral occipital cortex site (near PO7 electrode) and a right cingulate gyrus site (near Fz electrode) via averaged FC maps from 1000 healthy individuals, providing a reproducible, population-level candidate stimulation target framework in contrast to the highly variable individual-level targets.
Anxiety level was identified as the top predictor of post-COVID fatigue in the Random Forest model.
BMI was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue identified by the Random Forest model.
Depression level was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue in the Random Forest model.
Post-COVID increased irritability was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue.
Memory issues were among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue in the Random Forest model.
A history of fatty liver disease was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue.
Tingling in the hands and feet was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue, suggesting a possible small fiber neuropathy component.
Post-COVID excessive sweating was among the top predictors of post-COVID fatigue, suggesting autonomic involvement.
The Random Forest model outperformed Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, and Decision Trees in predicting post-COVID fatigue, achieving 85% accuracy.
Data mining identified 37 factors significantly associated with post-COVID fatigue among the cohort's variables.
Serum HSP90α levels did not differ significantly between long-COVID cases and recovered controls.
Serum Serpin F1 (PEDF) levels did not differ significantly between long-COVID cases and recovered controls.
Serum hemopexin levels did not differ significantly between long-COVID cases and recovered controls.
Serum apolipoprotein A4 levels did not differ significantly between long-COVID cases and recovered controls.
CRP levels did not differ significantly between long-COVID cases and recovered controls.
TNF-α levels showed a non-significant trend toward being higher in long-COVID cases compared to recovered controls.
IL-6 levels showed a non-significant trend toward being higher in long-COVID cases compared to recovered controls.
IL-1β could not be analyzed because concentrations were predominantly below the lower limit of detection in this cohort.

Low-titer ANA positivity was slightly more frequent in long-COVID cases than recovered controls but did not reach statistical significance, and ANA status did not influence biomarker levels or fatigue severity.
Long-COVID cases reported markedly greater fatigue on the Fatigue Visual Analog Scale (fVAS) than recovered controls.
Long-COVID cases had substantially lower FACIT-F scores (indicating more severe fatigue) than recovered controls.
Long-COVID cases scored substantially lower on the SF-36 vitality subscale (worse fatigue/energy) than recovered controls.
Depressive symptoms (HADS-D) were significantly higher in long-COVID cases than in recovered controls.

Fatigue levels (fVAS and SF-36 vitality subscale) in recovered COVID controls were comparable to a pre-pandemic healthy control population, supporting recovered controls as a non-fatigued comparator group.
Unexpectedly, HADS-D depression scores were significantly lower in recovered COVID controls than in pre-pandemic healthy controls.
Multivariable regression models found no significant associations between age, sex, HSP90α, CRP, TNF-α or IL-6 and fatigue severity (fVAS, FACIT-F, SF-36 VS, HADS-D) in long-COVID patients.
In univariable analysis, older age showed a near-significant trend toward greater fatigue severity on the FACIT-F scale within the long-COVID group.
In univariable analysis, female sex showed a non-significant trend toward lower fVAS (less fatigue) score in long-COVID cases.
Linear polarizance (PL) was significantly higher in healthy skin than in pooled EDS (cEDS+hEDS) biopsies, suggesting more uniformly aligned collagen fibers in healthy tissue.

The β parameter (a measure of circular birefringence/optical rotation) was significantly greater in healthy tissue than in pooled EDS biopsies, suggesting reduced anisotropic effects in EDS-related structural alterations.

Circular retardance (ψ) showed a statistically significant difference between healthy and EDS skin, though values in both groups clustered near zero and the sign shift driving significance was attributable to only two deviating measurements, limiting confidence in a reproducible biological effect.

No statistically significant differences were found between healthy and EDS skin for total retardance (R) or its linear component (δ), consistent with total retardance being dominated by the linear component.
PL remained statistically significantly different between hEDS and cEDS biopsies, though with weaker discriminative strength than in the healthy-vs-EDS comparison.

rL values were significantly higher in hEDS than cEDS biopsies, with stronger statistical significance than PL, potentially reflecting differences in microstructural organization affecting polarization behavior.
P1 values were significantly greater in hEDS compared with cEDS samples, possibly indicating enhanced contributions from non-retardance-related optical effects.
P3 values were significantly greater in hEDS compared with cEDS samples.

Ptms values, reflecting deviation from mirror-transverse symmetry, were significantly greater in hEDS compared with cEDS samples, possibly indicating asymmetries in polarization responses orthogonal to light propagation.
The patient carried a novel compound heterozygous COL12A1 variant causing myopathic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with markedly decreased collagen XII levels on muscle biopsy and immunostaining.
RNA sequencing showed near absence of the long collagen XII isoform with residual expression of the short isoform, which may explain the patient's clinical improvement over time.
The patient's mEDS was complicated by Chiari I malformation and hydrocephalus, a feature suggested to help distinguish mEDS from COL6-related myopathic EDS disorders.
Among the six women with vEDS diagnosed before pregnancy, no maternal deaths and no aortic dissections occurred during pregnancy or postpartum.
Combining serial aortic measurements from women with more than two measurements, there was no statistically significant aortic growth at the sinus of Valsalva or ascending aorta across pregnancy.
Obstetric complications were common, occurring in 80% of the pregnancies in this vEDS cohort.
One fetal death (stillbirth at 24 weeks gestation, cause unknown) occurred among the six pregnancies, representing 16.7% of cases.
Four out of five (80%) patients with live deliveries underwent caesarean section specifically because of their vEDS diagnosis.
Aortic complications specifically have been reported as more prevalent in vEDS patients carrying haplo-insufficient COL3A1 variants, and none of the six patients in this series had that variant type.

In-frame insertion-deletion variants located in the collagen helical domain of COL3A1 (patients 3 and 4) and glycine substitution variants (patients 1, 5 and 6) are both reported to be associated with a more severe vEDS phenotype.

A prior prospective randomised trial in non-pregnant French and Belgian vEDS patients found that celiprolol use was associated with reduced rates of aortic dissection, forming the basis for ESC guideline recommendations during pregnancy.

A separate prior study using Kaplan-Meier survival curves found similar overall survival between ever-pregnant and never-pregnant women with vEDS, suggesting pregnancy does not alter overall survival.
A recent systematic review of 412 vEDS pregnancies reported a maternal mortality rate of 5.7% and a major complication (vascular/uterine/intestinal rupture) rate of 5.4%.
A recent systematic review found that the premature delivery rate in vEDS pregnancies (7.3%) is similar to the global prematurity rate.
In this cohort, three out of five (60%) live infants were delivered prematurely, comprising one emergency CS for PPROM with contractions and two planned CS at 35 and 36 weeks.

Three patients who breastfed their infants (for 30 weeks, two months, and unspecified duration) experienced no complications, suggesting breastfeeding may be safe in vEDS, though numbers are too small to draw firm conclusions.

Individually, Patient 1 (with a glycine substitution variant) showed a 5 mm increase at the sinus of Valsalva and a 6 mm increase at the aortic arch across serial imaging during and after pregnancy, while Patient 4 (in-frame indel variant) did not show major increases.

Among 20 pediatric 21-OHD patients screened by long-read sequencing, 2 (10%) were identified with characteristic EDS manifestations (Beighton score ≥5) and pathogenic TNXB variants, confirming CAH-X syndrome.

Patient 1 carried a novel CAH-X genotype caused by a large gene conversion spanning from CYP21A2 exon 4 to TNXB intron 33 (chr6:32039426–32044184), incorporating multiple pseudogene-derived pathogenic variants in both genes on one allele, without the typical 30-kb deletion.
Patient 2 was found by LRS to carry a TNXA/TNXB_CH-1 chimeric gene on one allele, confirming a diagnosis of CAH-X syndrome with a phenotype limited mainly to joint hypermobility.

The CAH-X CH-1 chimera's 120-bp deletion (c.11435_11524+30del) in TNXB exon 35 reduces TNX expression through haploinsufficiency, whereas CH-2 and CH-3 chimeras retain expression but alter protein structure via dominant-negative effects.
Two patients (P3, P4) carried TNXB variants classified as VUS or likely benign but had Beighton scores of 0 and no EDS-related signs, and were therefore not diagnosed with CAH-X syndrome.
The remaining 16 of 20 patients had Beighton scores not exceeding 3 (average 1.0) and no pathogenic TNXB variants, consistent with absence of an EDS phenotype.

The father of Patient 1, a heterozygous carrier of the novel CAH-X genotype without 21-OHD, showed no EDS-related symptoms and had a Beighton score of 0, consistent with the milder phenotype expected in heterozygous carriers.
The c.188A>T and c.208G>T CYP21A2 variants were associated with the non-classical (NC) and simple-virilizing (SV) types of 21-OHD phenotype, respectively.

Compared with studies outside of China reporting that nearly 100% of 21-OHD patients with CAH-X chimeric genes exhibit EDS-related symptoms, Chinese cohort data showed only a 71% prevalence, suggesting a comparatively milder EDS phenotype in Chinese patients with CAH-X syndrome.
A cited study (Wang et al.) found that targeted long-read sequencing provided a more precise diagnosis in 14.6% of CAH cases compared with standard molecular diagnostic methods.

A cited study (Liu et al.) reported that LRS-based assays determined all CAH genotypes with 100% sensitivity and specificity, outperforming MLPA and Sanger sequencing in resolving complex alleles and cis-trans configurations.

This study concludes that long-read sequencing is a reliable method for genetic diagnosis of CAH-X syndrome, resolving complex RCCX rearrangements that are missed by Sanger sequencing, MLPA, and standard NGS.
Prior literature indicates that approximately 10% to 15% of patients with 21-hydroxylase deficiency have concurrent defects in CYP21A2 and TNXB genes, resulting in CAH-X syndrome.

Patient 1 exhibited generalized joint hypermobility (Beighton score ≥6), fragile skin, easy bruising, and borderline skin hyperextensibility, consistent with a mild EDS phenotype associated with her novel CAH-X genotype.

An older woman with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome and severe opioid use disorder on 280 MME/day was successfully transitioned to buprenorphine-naloxone via a 7-day outpatient micro-induction protocol with minimal withdrawal symptoms.

The authors suggest outpatient buprenorphine micro-induction can be safely implemented in older adults with chronic opioid exposure, especially those obtaining prescription opioids from outside prescribers, supported by pharmacogenomics, trauma-informed care, and interdisciplinary coordination.
The case report describes bilateral vertebral artery aneurysms causing symptomatic Bow Hunter's syndrome attributed to C1-2 cervical spine hypermobility.

This systematic review of sickness absence duration across twenty prevalent work-disability pathologies found no studies reporting sickness absence duration data for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, alongside epilepsy and obsessive compulsive disorder.

Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (type 4) is cited as a condition in which arterial catheter access carries higher risk, making intravenous 3D-DSA an acceptable noninvasive substitute for cerebrovascular imaging.
Among 528 adult IV 3D-DSA cases, only 7 (1.3%) were significantly limited by motion artifact and just 3 (0.6%) were considered nondiagnostic.
No significant complications were reported across the 549 IV 3D-DSA procedures performed.
The primary indication for IV 3D-DSA was aneurysm evaluation (initial, postoperative, or follow-up) in 408 of 528 adult patients and 9 of 21 pediatric patients.

Nearly all pediatric IV 3D-DSA cases (20 of 21) required general anesthesia, compared with only 86 of 528 adult cases (most performed intraoperatively under the same anesthetic as the index operation).

In the neutral (non-stress) ankle position, ATFL shear wave velocity at the middle segment was significantly lower in the High-BS (high joint hypermobility) group compared to the Low-BS group after Bonferroni correction.
In the neutral position, no significant between-group difference in ATFL SWV was found at the proximal or distal segments after Bonferroni correction.
Under maximal plantar-flexion-inversion (stress) position, ATFL SWV at the proximal segment was significantly lower in the High-BS group than in the Low-BS group.
Under maximal plantar-flexion-inversion (stress) position, ATFL SWV at the distal segment was significantly lower in the High-BS group than in the Low-BS group.
The middle segment difference in stress position did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction.
No significant correlations were found between ATFL SWV and demographic variables (age, height, weight, BMI, ATFL length, foot length) in either the High-BS or Low-BS group.

Baseline demographic and anthropometric characteristics (age, weight, height, BMI, foot length, ATFL length) were comparable between the High-BS and Low-BS groups, indicating BS variation was not driven by body-size characteristics.
Intra-observer reliability of ATFL SWV measurements was good to excellent across all ligament segments and ankle positions in both BS groups.

Overall, mean ATFL SWV was approximately 10% lower in the high-BS (hypermobile) group compared to the low-BS group, indicating an inverse association between generalized joint hypermobility and ligament stiffness.

MRI-measured internal rotational tibial subluxation greater than 5.5 mm is associated with high-grade (grade 2-3) pivot shift instability in ACL-deficient knees, with excellent specificity for high-grade instability.
MRI-measured axial internal tibial rotation greater than 8.1 degrees is associated with high-grade (grade 2-3) pivot shift instability in ACL-deficient knees.
Patient hypermobility is listed as one of the consensus indications for adding a lateral extra-articular procedure (LEAP) to ACL reconstruction.
Three-corner TMT arthrodesis achieved greater initial intermetatarsal angle correction at 6 weeks postoperatively compared to single first TMT arthrodesis.
Early loss of intermetatarsal angle correction between 6 weeks and 6 months was greater after single first TMT arthrodesis than after three-corner TMT arthrodesis.
Both single first TMT arthrodesis and three-corner TMT arthrodesis produced significant correction of hallux valgus radiographic parameters overall.
The change in pelvic-femoral angle between standing and flexed-seated positions (ΔPFA) discriminated simulated prosthetic impingement at 40/20° cup orientation with good accuracy.
A ΔPFA threshold of 110° showed high specificity and NPV but modest sensitivity for identifying impingement risk, marking a small high-risk subgroup.
Patients with ΔPFA ≥110° had markedly higher rates of adverse spinopelvic mobility (ΔSPT ≥20°) than those with lower ΔPFA.
ΔPFA ≥110° was associated with substantially higher simulated impingement rates at the 40/15° cup orientation.
ΔPFA ≥110° was associated with substantially higher simulated impingement rates at the 40/20° cup orientation.
Patients with ΔPFA ≥110° had a much smaller impingement-free anteversion safe-zone width than those below the threshold.
In multivariable analysis, ΔSPT ≥20° independently predicted simulated impingement at 40/20° cup orientation.
In multivariable logistic regression, ΔPFA ≥110° independently predicted simulated impingement at 40/20° even after accounting for spinopelvic mobility.

Among patients with ΔPFA ≥110°, the phenotype defined by low flexed-seated PFA alone (≤90°) showed the highest rate of corridor collapse (loss of an impingement-free anteversion zone) and the highest impingement rates at both simulated angles.
Very low flexed-seated pelvic-femoral angle, especially below 80-85°, identified extreme hyperflexion outliers who frequently lacked any impingement-free anteversion corridor.
The authors conclude that combining ΔPFA thresholding with flexed-seated PFA phenotyping may help refine patient-specific cup orientation planning before total hip arthroplasty.
Pain scores improved significantly after arthroscopic inferior capsular shift surgery for atraumatic (type II) shoulder instability.
SPONSA shoulder function scores improved significantly after surgery, indicating better perceived shoulder normality.
Oxford Shoulder Score improved from pre- to post-operative assessment following capsular shift surgery.
Post-operative Oxford Shoulder Instability score of 34.6 indicated 'good' shoulder stability following surgery.
Despite surgery, 39% of patients reported continued or recurrent instability symptoms, a higher rate than previously reported in the literature.
5 of 59 followed-up patients (8.5%) required revision stabilization surgery after the index procedure.
Age under 30 was a significant predictor of recurrent instability after surgery in this atraumatic cohort.
Female gender was a significant predictor of recurrent instability after arthroscopic capsular shift surgery.
Beighton hypermobility score was not predictive of post-operative recurrence, despite hypermobility being prevalent in the cohort.
Direction of pre-operative instability (anterior, inferior, posterior, multidirectional) was not a significant predictor of post-operative recurrence.
14 of 70 patients undergoing surgery for atraumatic shoulder instability had a pre-existing connective tissue disorder such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
One patient developed adhesive capsulitis as a post-operative complication, requiring further arthroscopic capsular release surgery.
Patients who ultimately required revision surgery had worse pre-operative-to-outcome scores (pain, SPONSA, OSS) than those who did not.
Ten of 14 pediatric patients undergoing combined MPFL/MPTL reconstruction for fixed or obligatory patellar dislocation had a history of genetic, syndromic, or hypermobility conditions.
Concomitant MPFL and MPTL reconstruction resulted in only one recurrent patellar dislocation postoperatively out of 16 extremities over an average follow-up of 25 months.

Preoperative MRI showed an elevated mean tibial tuberosity-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance, with seven of sixteen extremities exceeding 20 mm, a threshold associated with abnormal patellofemoral alignment.
Among the 16 extremities studied, fixed patellar dislocations were present in 9 and obligatory patellar dislocations in 7.

Rats fed the gut-microbiota acetogenic diet (GMAD) prior to reserpine injection did not develop mechanical allodynia, whereas control-diet rats showed a marked drop in paw withdrawal threshold after reserpine.
GMAD accelerated resolution of reserpine-induced tactile (dynamic brush) allodynia, which fully resolved by day 12 in GMAD rats but remained elevated in control-diet rats.
GMAD provided significant protection against reserpine-induced cold hypersensitivity compared with control diet.
Reserpine-induced cold allodynia was seen only in female rats, with no significant change observed in males.
Reserpine injection did not induce heat/thermal hypersensitivity in the Hargreaves test, and GMAD had no effect on this measure.
No group showed motor coordination deficits on the rotarod test, confirming that reduced pain-like behaviors were not due to motor impairment.
GMAD dramatically increased relative abundance of Bacteroidales bacterium in the fecal microbiome, an acetate-producing taxon.
GMAD significantly promoted growth of Bifidobacterium animalis, an acetate/lactate-producing bacterium via the bifidus shunt pathway.
GMAD increased relative abundance of Bacteroides ovatus, another acetate-producing bacterium.
GMAD significantly reduced abundance of butyrate-producing bacteria Lachnospiraceae bacterium and Butyrivibrio.
GMAD significantly reduced abundance of the mucin-degrading specialist Akkermansia muciniphila.
GMAD-fed rats had significantly higher circulating serum acetate concentrations than control-diet rats at day 13.
Beta-diversity (community structure) of the gut microbiome differed significantly between GMAD and control-diet groups, while alpha diversity and body weight were unchanged.
GMAD significantly increased IL-10 mRNA expression in the dorsal root ganglia of the reserpine-induced fibromyalgia model.
GMAD significantly increased IL-10 mRNA expression in the lumbar spinal cord of R-iFM rats.
GMAD significantly increased IL-2 mRNA expression in the spinal cord of R-iFM rats, a novel finding for acetate action.
GMAD significantly increased IL-6 mRNA expression in the spinal cord of both sham and R-iFM rats, interpreted here as a pro-resolution/neuroprotective rather than pro-inflammatory signal.
Reserpine induced a shift toward activated (hypertrophic) microglial morphology in the spinal dorsal horn, which was prevented by GMAD, restoring predominantly ramified/resting morphology.
GMAD significantly increased the percentage of resting (ramified) microglia in R-iFM rats compared to control-diet R-iFM rats, indicating a shift toward a quiescent state.
R-iFM increased mRNA expression of microglial markers IBA1 and CD68 in spinal cord, which GMAD suppressed back to sham-comparable levels.
GMAD prevented reserpine-induced upregulation of the reactive astrocyte marker GFAP in spinal cord, reducing it to baseline.
GMAD reduced the proportion of dorsal horn neurons exhibiting a T-type calcium channel-driven hyperexcitable (AP-after-hyperpolarization) firing phenotype in R-iFM rats.
GMAD caused hyperpolarization of resting membrane potential and reduced input resistance in dorsal horn neurons of R-iFM rats, indicating reduced intrinsic excitability restored toward sham levels.
Spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP) frequency, elevated in R-iFM control-diet rats, was significantly reduced by GMAD to sham-like levels.
Reserpine-induced cold allodynia occurred only in female rats, with no significant cold hypersensitivity seen in males.

In the reserpine model on control diet, spontaneous glycinergic inhibitory current frequency was reduced compared to sham, and this reduction was reversed by pharmacological blockade of the PGE2 EP2 receptor with PF-04418948.

Blocking the EP2 receptor with PF-04418948 significantly increased evoked glycinergic IPSC amplitude in dorsal horn neurons from the control-diet R-iFM group, but had no effect in sham groups or in GMAD-fed R-iFM rats, indicating GMAD prevents PGE2-mediated glycinergic disinhibition.
The discussion notes that GMAD enriched additional acetate-producing taxa including Phocaeicola vulgatus, alongside Bacteroidales bacterium and Bacteroides ovatus.

In long COVID, increased kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratios and insulin resistance correlate with the severity of physiosomatic and affective symptoms.

Lactate acts as a signaling metabolite that stabilizes HIF-1α via PHD2 interaction, upregulating IL-1β in macrophages and promoting pro-inflammatory adipose tissue responses independent of BMI.

Lipidomic studies in ME/CFS reveal sex-specific alterations in phospholipids, ceramides, and oxylipins correlating with severity of fatigue and pain.

Molecular hydrogen has been investigated for anti-fatigue effects in human and exercise-related settings via proposed antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
Red ginseng extract has been associated with improved skeletal muscle energy metabolism and mitochondrial function in experimental fatigue models.

The study reports platelet functional defects identified in both human patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and a mouse model of the disease.
Genetic testing identified a pathogenic COL3A1 mutation confirming the diagnosis of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in this patient.

Lung histopathology showed perivascular cuffing, haemosiderin-laden macrophages and fibrosis without vasculitis or malignancy, and special stains for amyloid, mycobacteria and fungi were negative.
Empirical anti-tuberculosis therapy was given for 6 months despite negative special stains, and was later considered unnecessary once vascular EDS was diagnosed.

Chest CT in 2020 revealed calcified and ossified dendriform parenchymal bands with cystic degeneration and marked mosaic attenuation with air trapping, findings the authors note have been described previously in vascular EDS.
Genetic testing identified a pathogenic COL3A1 mutation confirming the diagnosis of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in this patient.
Skin biopsy from the lower extremity showed calcified and fragmented elastic fibers resembling pseudoxanthoma elasticum (PXE) histopathology, despite the patient not carrying ABCC6-related PXE.

The patient presented with bilateral lower extremity sclerosis clinically resembling lipodermatosclerosis, but Doppler ultrasound showed no venous insufficiency, suggesting an alternative vEDS-related mechanism for the skin changes.
CT angiography revealed moderate stenosis of the superior mesenteric artery in this vEDS patient, without symptoms of mesenteric ischemia.
Treatment with potent topical steroids and pentoxifylline led to decreased skin tightness, reduced swelling, and improved nighttime discomfort over the following months.
Family history was notable for multiple relatives carrying a COL3A1 mutation and/or a history of perforated diverticulosis.

The patient-derived iPSC line JHUi009-A carries a pathogenic COL3A1 c.2456G>A variant, consistent with a diagnosis of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (vEDS).
iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs) from the COL3A1-mutant vEDS line showed higher expression of contractile marker proteins compared to the CRISPR-corrected isogenic control vSMCs.

Repeated measures ANOVA showed significant improvement across all patient-reported outcome measures over 24 months of CBMP treatment.

47.08% of patients reported clinically significant improvement on the SF-MPQ-2 by 24 months of CBMP treatment.

None of the patients experienced recurrent shoulder subluxations or dislocations after open capsular shift with Achilles allograft augmentation.

The authors cite a prior case series in which three of five patients with FKBP14-related Ehlers-Danlos syndrome had nephroptosis, attributed to underlying muscular weakness.

The three known TNXB chimeras (CH1: 120-bp deletion causing TNXB haploinsufficiency; CH2: p.Cys4058Trp missense causing severe EDS; CH3: three missense variants) are described as the molecular basis of CAH-X syndrome.
In the Munich CAH cohort (n=155), fewer than 5% of patients carried the CAH-X CH1 chimera (7 of 153 tested), lower than the 7%-15% frequency reported in other cohorts.
Among the seven CAH-X positive patients, six carried a monoallelic TNXA/TNXB chimera and one carried a biallelic chimera, the latter previously diagnosed with EDS.
Serum TNXB protein levels were modestly elevated in CAH-X patients compared with CAH control patients without the 120-bp deletion.
Both CAH-X and CAH control patients had lower serum TNXB levels than the average non-CAH population reference value.
The study found no correlation between serum TNXB protein levels and clinical observations, consistent with prior studies by Kolli et al. and Yamada et al.
Positive Beighton scores (joint hypermobility) were observed in three of five CAH-X patients (60%), specifically those with higher serum TNXB levels, while no control participant scored above 2.
All CAH-X case subjects reported back pain and foot malposition at least monthly, versus 40% of CAH control subjects, though the difference was not statistically significant.
CAH-X patients had significantly reduced skin thickness at the triceps compared to matched CAH control patients.
Three of five CAH-X patients (60%) showed increased muscle echogenicity on ultrasound, consistent with myopathy attributed to increased phosphorylated SMAD1/5/8 from abnormal BMP signaling.

CAH-X patients in groups 2 and 3 performed less efficiently in cardiovascular fitness step tests compared with matched CAH controls.
The single CAH-X patient carrying the biallelic chimera showed mild sensory impairment (Rydel-Seiffer vibration score 4-5) in the lower extremities, unlike all other participants who scored normally.
Muscle strength assessed by dynamometer in the dominant arm showed no significant difference between CAH-X and CAH control patients, though controls trended stronger.
One CAH-X patient (group 1) had a significantly higher pressure pain threshold than CAH control subjects, while other pain sensitivity assessments showed no significant abnormality.

The authors hypothesize that increased TGFβ2 activation resulting from TNXB deficiency may underlie the persistent truncus arteriosus and other cardiac abnormalities observed in CAH-X patients, based on prior mouse models linking TGFβ2 elevation with retinoic acid receptor deficiency and truncus arteriosus.

In the Marfan syndrome cohort, FBN1 variants were found in 96.8% of patients, and the majority (87.5%) had FBN1 variants coexisting with variants in other cardiovascular-disease genes.
Among 16 Loeys-Dietz syndrome patients, 81.2% had TGFBR2 variants and 18.8% had TGFBR1 variants, with 93.7% showing coexisting variants in other genes.
All 13 patients with Beals-Hecht syndrome (congenital contractural arachnodactyly) had a positive FBN2 variant, and all had coexisting variants in other genes.
Among 7 patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, causative variants were found in COL3A1 (57.1%), COL5A2 (28.5%), and COL5A1 (14.2%), and all patients had coexisting variants in additional genes.

In the undifferentiated connective tissue disease group (negative for FBN1/TGFBR1/TGFBR2/SMAD3/FBN2), sarcomere gene variants including MYBPC3 (25.7%), SDHA (20%), AKAP9 (14.2%), and RYR2 (14.2%) were the most frequent coexisting variants.
A recurrent MYBPC3 in-frame deletion (NM_000256.3:c.2440_2442del, p.Lys814del) was found across MS, LDS, BHS, and UCTD patients but was absent among the EDS patients.
In an age/sex-matched sub-analysis, MYBPC3-positive patients had a higher rate of aortic dissection (17.6%) and death (11.7%) than MYBPC3-negative patients, who had no dissection and no deaths.
In Marfan syndrome, patients with coexisting gene variants had numerically lower median LVEF than those without coexistence, but the difference was not statistically significant.
In Marfan syndrome, the proportion of patients with preserved LVEF was significantly lower in those with coexisting genetic variants than in those without.
In Loeys-Dietz syndrome, patients with coexisting gene variants also tended to have lower LVEF than those without, though the small sample precluded statistical testing.

In one Beals-Hecht syndrome patient with arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a coexisting FBN1 variant and a TTN variant of uncertain significance (rs770301886) were identified.

A 44-year-old man with Marfan syndrome carried a pathogenic FBN1 stop-codon variant (rs794728165) coexisting with an SCN5A variant, and presented with severe aortic dilation (84mm), bicuspid aortic valve, reduced ejection fraction (40%), and severe musculoskeletal deformity.
A 15-year-old patient with cardiac-vascular type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome had coexisting SDHA and COL5A2 variants with severe musculoskeletal and cardiovascular damage including bradyarrhythmia.

The paper describes that FBN1 variants impair fibrillin-1's normal role in sequestering TGF-β, leading to increased extracellular TGF-β bioavailability and loss of ECM homeostasis implicated in aortic wall damage in Marfan syndrome.

A patient with undifferentiated connective tissue disease and coexisting AKAP9 and COL5A2 variants had no significant cardiovascular imaging damage but presented with dysautonomia.
A patient with coexisting FBN1 and RBM20 variants (RBM20 regulating alternative splicing of titin) showed diffuse myocardial fibrosis on MRI, suggesting subclinical cardiac risk requiring evaluation.

MMPs and cysteine cathepsins modulate collagen structure and degradation, generating bioactive fragments used as clinical biomarkers.

Elastolytic proteases including cathepsins K, S, and V and MMP2/7/9/12 mediate physiological elastin remodeling but fuel pathological states when dysregulated, releasing elastin-derived peptides that act as signaling matrikines.
The review highlights novel therapeutic strategies, including substrate- and exosite-selective protease inhibitors, aimed at restoring ECM homeostasis while minimizing off-target effects.

Multivariable regression showed GJH was independently correlated with larger thoracic kyphosis in AIS patients.

No significant differences in patient-reported outcome measures (SRS-22r) were observed between GJH and non-GJH AIS patients postoperatively.

Observed Harris Hip Scores were significantly lower in GJH patients than non-GJH patients at 1, 3, and 6 months after THA, but the difference was no longer significant at 12 months or final follow-up.

Subgroup analysis restricted to studies using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry confirmed lower 25(OH)D in GP children.
Across four observational studies, vitamin D supplementation in children with growing pains significantly increased serum 25(OH)D and reduced pain intensity over 1-24 months.
Two small case-control studies found higher prevalence of hypovitaminosis D and lower vitamin D levels in GP cases versus controls, but the differences were not statistically significant.
A Korean retrospective study of 140 children with GP found a 57.1% prevalence of vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency.
A Pakistani cross-sectional study of 100 children with GP found a 94% prevalence of vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency.
Multifactor logistic regression showed children with GP who received vitamin D supplementation had a lower risk of pain lasting ≥30 minutes.

In a 5-year follow-up cohort, bone strength increased over time in GP patients with no significant difference between those with resolved GP and those with continuing episodes; pain alleviation paralleled bone strength increases.
Meta-analysis of two studies found physical activity was a significant risk factor for growth pain disorder.

Joint hypermobility was significantly more prevalent among children with growing pains than among children without growing pains.
A study comparing foot posture and functional health between children with and without GP found no meaningful relationship, failing to support the anatomical etiology theory.
In a case-control study, increased ankle dorsiflexion strength predicted membership in the GP subgroup.

A single-case experimental design in eight children with GP and pronated foot posture found symptom amelioration with triplane wedges or orthoses, with milder symptom recurrence after treatment withdrawal.
A retrospective study found that children with higher insole compliance and posterior orientation experienced greater pain relief than those with lower compliance or anterior orientation.
Multivariate regression analysis identified family history as a significant risk factor for growth pain disorder.

Logistic regression revealed asocial behavior was a risk factor for growing pain duration ≥30 minutes, while nervousness, anxiety, and inattention were not significantly associated.
Li et al. found that children with GP had significantly lower pain thresholds around the knee and more tender points at specific anatomical sites compared with controls.
Hashkes et al. reported decreased pain thresholds at fibromyalgia tender points, control points, and the anterior tibia in children with GP.
At 5-year follow-up, children with persistent GP maintained significantly lower pain thresholds compared with both healthy controls and children whose GP had resolved.

Logistic regression identified asocial behavior as a risk factor for GP pain lasting ≥30 minutes, while other psychological factors (nervousness, anxiety, inattention) were not significantly associated with pain duration.
Parents rated children with GP as more likely to have negative mood, aggression, anxiety, and hyperactivity than control children.
Perinatal anthropometric parameters (gestational age, birth length, birth weight, head circumference) were robustly correlated with GP severity.
Breastfeeding status and duration correlated significantly with GP onset in infancy, but did not affect pain type or frequency in children with confirmed GP.
Picky eating was identified as a risk factor for GP in a case-control study.
Obesity prevalence was significantly higher among children with GP than among healthy controls.
No conclusive evidence was found linking parent-child bed-sharing, vascular perfusion patterns, fatty acid status, or rapid growth to childhood GP.
Persistent GP episodes were significantly more prevalent in children with a family history of pain syndromes, suggesting genetics may modulate pain thresholds via pain perception pathway sensitivity.

A multidimensional symptom burden model (including pain catastrophizing, physical function, sleep, anxiety, depression, hypermobility, and quantitative sensory testing) explained 75% of the variance in pain intensity/interference (PEG) in the overall sample, 82% in the active myofascial pain group, and 92% in the normal (pain-free) group.
PROMIS physical function (PF) and pain catastrophizing (PCS) were identified as key predictors of pain intensity/interference (PEG) among people with unexplained neck/shoulder myofascial pain.
Network analysis of symptom and outcome variables identified distinct symptom clusters that differed between the active and latent myofascial pain groups.
Joint hypermobility was identified as one of the main risk factors for musculoskeletal injuries in classical ballet dancers, reported in 10 of the 46 included studies.

Across the included studies, the ankle and foot were the most frequently affected body regions for musculoskeletal injuries in classical ballet dancers, with lower limb injuries predominating overall.
Overload was identified as the main risk factor for musculoskeletal injuries in classical ballet dancers, reported in 17 of the included studies.
Among 1269 SARD patients reporting fibromyalgia status, 25.9% (n=329) reported a co-diagnosis of fibromyalgia.
Over half of patients with a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis (52.8%) expressed doubt or uncertainty about its accuracy, with only 47.1% fully accepting the diagnosis.
SARD patients with a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis reported significantly lower confidence in receiving needed medical help compared to those without fibromyalgia.
SARD patients with a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis reported significantly less trust in their GPs and rheumatologists than those without the diagnosis.

Despite poorer wellbeing measures, SARD patients with a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis rated their current health as significantly better than those without fibromyalgia, a paradox the authors attribute to reattribution of persisting symptoms.
Patients with fibromyalgia reported significantly lower life satisfaction and satisfaction with medical care compared to those without the diagnosis.
Patients with fibromyalgia reported significantly lower disease adaptation and perceived control compared to those without fibromyalgia.
No significant difference in self-reported disease knowledge was found between SARD patients with and without a fibromyalgia diagnosis.
SARD patients with a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis had significantly poorer wellbeing across all WEMWBS items, resulting in a significantly lower total wellbeing score.
Among fibromyalgia-diagnosed patients, those who accepted their diagnosis had lived with their SARD diagnosis significantly longer than those who felt misdiagnosed.
Fibromyalgia patients who accepted their diagnosis reported better current health and greater satisfaction with care than those who felt misdiagnosed.
No significant differences in years to diagnosis or years since diagnosis of the primary autoimmune condition were observed between patients with and without a fibromyalgia co-diagnosis.

Qualitative data showed patients consistently struggled to distinguish fibromyalgia symptoms from those of their SARD due to overlapping pain, fatigue, and cognitive dysfunction, and the absence of definitive diagnostic biomarkers.

Clinicians interviewed showed marked variability in how they conceptualised fibromyalgia's aetiology, ranging from neurological/central pain processing to stress-related, depressive, or coping-based explanations, with some questioning its existence as a distinct entity.

Patients reported that after receiving a fibromyalgia diagnosis, clinicians were less likely to pursue further investigations, sometimes resulting in delayed identification of serious underlying pathology (e.g., lupus-related brain damage, renal flare).
Many participants perceived fibromyalgia as a 'catch-all' or 'bucket' diagnosis applied when blood tests were negative or inconclusive, used to close investigation rather than explain symptoms.

Clinicians and patients described a gendered dynamic in which women's pain associated with fibromyalgia was frequently minimised or reframed as stress/coping-related, reinforcing feelings of dismissal.
Depressed Mood showed the highest bridge centrality among symptoms connecting fibromyalgia and depression symptom clusters.
Fatigue was identified as a key bridge symptom linking fibromyalgia and depression symptom clusters, and also linked to Pain Severity.
Anxiety & Nervousness was identified as one of the top bridge symptoms connecting fibromyalgia and depression symptom clusters.

Pain Severity showed surprisingly minimal connectivity within the symptom network, ranking 18th in bridge strength and linking mainly to Sleeping Problems and Fatigue, contrary to its assumed central role in FMS-MDD comorbidity.

Network analysis of 30 symptom nodes revealed seven distinct symptom clusters spanning pain/functional impact, autonomic/somatic complaints, trauma/anxiety, sexual/health concerns, anhedonia/social disconnection, cognitive-affective/psychomotor dysfunction, and sleep/energy/social functioning domains.
Across ALFF, fALFF, and ReHo analyses, chronic pain patients showed consistent abnormalities in the thalamus and precuneus compared with healthy controls.
The ACC showed both state-dependent functional connectivity abnormalities and structural (gray matter volume) alterations in chronic pain patients relative to controls.

The postcentral gyrus showed concurrent ReHo and VBM abnormalities and the superior parietal gyrus showed altered VBM, indicating combined functional and structural sensorimotor network abnormalities in chronic pain.

Concurrent ReHo and degree centrality abnormalities in the SMA suggest disrupted local neuronal synchrony and reduced network hub efficiency in chronic pain patients, potentially impairing motor preparation and descending pain modulation.
Disrupted ReHo in the SPL and IPL, higher-order somatosensory association areas, indicates dysregulated somatosensory attention allocation and spatial processing under chronic pain conditions.
Abnormal ALFF and ReHo within the insula, along with altered functional connectivity to multiple regions, suggest impaired sensory integration and emotional regulation functions in chronic pain.
The thalamus shows widespread local abnormalities and altered functional connectivity with the ACC, reflecting a thalamocortical axis implicated in pain-emotion integration.
Abnormal local amplitude metrics (ALFF/fALFF) in the RVM provide indirect support for state-dependent functional decline in the descending pain inhibitory pathway in chronic pain patients.
Multiple prior studies cited in this review reported reduced activity and connectivity within the DMN in patients with chronic pain.
Following acupuncture intervention, the precuneus showed significant pre- versus post-treatment changes across ALFF, fALFF, and ReHo, mirroring its baseline abnormality in chronic pain.
FC analyses repeatedly identified the left postcentral gyrus, right cerebellum, and right inferior occipital gyrus as regions with significantly altered functional connectivity after acupuncture.
In RCTs comparing verum with sham acupuncture, verum acupuncture produced significantly greater FC alterations in the left MTG and right amygdala across multiple studies.
Verum acupuncture produced significantly greater ACC and STG changes than sham acupuncture, jointly implicated by ReHo and task-based fMRI analyses.
In RCTs where sham acupuncture produced greater brain changes than verum acupuncture, the SPL, MFG, and right insula showed significant changes across multiple FC analyses.

The MFG's sensitivity to sham acupuncture was corroborated across three distinct modalities (ReHo, VBM, and task-fMRI), highlighting pronounced structural and functional changes with sham stimulation.

Enhanced-expectancy acupuncture (EEA), relative to standard acupuncture or usual care, was associated with altered functional connectivity centered on the nucleus accumbens involving cingulate/prefrontal and somatosensory regions, suggesting engagement of reward/expectancy processing.

Within-group pre- versus post-sham-acupuncture analysis revealed significant FC changes between bilateral MFG, suggesting sham acupuncture responses may involve cognitive control changes beyond transient activation.

Verum acupuncture, relative to sham, was associated with significantly enhanced ACC functional connectivity with the VTA and left posterior medial PFC, plus ReHo and task-activation differences, suggesting engagement of prefrontal-limbic reward and pain-appraisal networks.

Verum acupuncture significantly enhanced functional connectivity between the amygdala and the median raphe, VTA, and periaqueductal gray compared with sham acupuncture, suggesting stronger engagement of limbic-brainstem descending pain modulatory pathways.
The global consensus-2 diagnostic criteria, established in 2020, have increased recognition and diagnosis of MCAS, which had previously been underdiagnosed by more restrictive criteria.

Consensus-2 criteria have enabled diagnosis and effective treatment for many MCAS patients previously labeled with unexplained inflammatory syndromes or misdiagnosed with somatization or other primary psychiatric disorders.
Concerns that the broader consensus-2 criteria would lead to overdiagnosis of MCAS have not materialized.
Appropriate therapy for MCAS can dramatically improve quality of life, sometimes reversing decades of morbidity and disability that persisted despite extensive prior unhelpful workups and treatments.
The spectrum of diseases thought to be rooted in variants of MCAS, or to which MCAS significantly contributes, continues to expand, indicating broad comorbidity and heterogeneity of the disease.

The patient was found to have a heterozygous CACNA1S missense variant (p.Ala1282Ser), an ultra-rare, previously unreported variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance located in transmembrane domain III.

The p.Ala1282Ser variant has conflicting interpretations of pathogenicity in ClinVar, and an automated ACMG re-evaluation predicted a likely benign classification, though the authors retained a VUS designation given phenotype compatibility.

Multiple sequence alignment showed alanine at position 1282 is strictly conserved across mammalian and teleost fish CACNA1S orthologs within transmembrane domain III, supporting potential functional importance of this residue.
Citing a prior study (Afrin et al.), the authors note that MCAS patients commonly experience fatigue (83%) and presyncope (71%), symptoms also reported by this patient.
According to the cited study, 41% of MCAS patients demonstrated hypokalemia during acute episodes, likely due to transcellular potassium shifts.
The patient had low renin and an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio, but primary hyperaldosteronism was considered unlikely given normal blood pressure and low-normal 24-hour urine aldosterone.
Initial laboratory workup revealed a positive ANA in this patient with MCAS and suspected hKPP.
The patient was started on oral potassium supplementation and trialed on spironolactone as maintenance therapy but did not tolerate the medication.
CACNA1S mutations account for an estimated 60%-80% of hKPP cases, SCN4A mutations for 15%-20%, with etiology unclear in the remaining 10%-15%.
hKPP shows a marked male predominance (male-to-female ratio 3:1 to 4:1), attributed to higher penetrance in males likely due to sex hormone modulation of ion channel activity.
The long exercise test, a repetitive nerve stimulation test, has shown sensitivity up to 95% and specificity 71%-95% for confirming hKPP in patients with frequent attacks.
The patient's recurrent dizziness and fatigue episodes led her to discontinue driving and rely on public transportation, illustrating significant functional impact of her condition.
Active vitiligo lesions and skin from chronic restraint stress (CRS)-treated mice showed increased substance P-positive sensory innervation together with increased mast cell numbers.
Intradermal injection of full-length substance P or its SP1-9 proteolytic fragment, but not the SP1-7 fragment, activated mast cells and worsened depigmentation in the mouse vitiligo model.
Unlike SP and SP1-9, the SP1-7 fragment did not activate mast cells or worsen depigmentation.
MrgprB2 knockout mice showed reduced melanocyte loss and reduced CD8+ T cell infiltration compared with wild-type mice in the Tyrp2 peptide-induced vitiligo model.
Silencing MRGPRX2 in mast cells abolished IFNγ production in response to substance P stimulation.
Keratinocyte-derived MMP9, but not fibroblast-derived neprilysin, preferentially generated the pro-inflammatory SP1-9 fragment from substance P as shown by LC-MS/MS profiling.
Fibroblast-derived neprilysin did not preferentially generate the pro-inflammatory SP1-9 fragment, in contrast to keratinocyte-derived MMP9.
Feeding neonatal mice an amino acid-based diet increased intestinal epithelial-derived IL-33 expression compared to controls before allergen challenge.
Amino acid-diet-fed mice showed intestinal mast cell activation upon oral ovalbumin challenge, indicating a mast-cell-driven allergic response.
Mice fed the amino acid-based diet had increased OVA-specific IgE and IgG1 levels after oral allergen challenge compared to controls.
Amino acid-diet feeding reduced the frequency of peripheral regulatory T cells (p-Tregs), impairing oral tolerance induction.
The amino acid-based diet led to expansion of the cDC2B dendritic cell subset alongside Th2 cells, contributing to a Th2-skewed immune response.

Long-term amino acid-based diet feeding in neonatal mice significantly impaired the generation of oral tolerance to the egg allergen ovalbumin, driving a Th2-dominant response and increasing food allergy susceptibility.
Adverse events from gadolinium-based contrast agents are uncommon, occurring in 0.04-0.3% of administrations, with 0.4-9% of these classified as severe.
Patients with a prior hypersensitivity reaction to gadolinium contrast have a 30% chance of experiencing another hypersensitivity episode on re-exposure.
Among patients who experienced an allergic, hypersensitive, anaphylactic, or anaphylactoid insult, Kounis syndrome prevalence ranged from 1.1% to 3.4%.
Type I Kounis syndrome (myocardial ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries) affects 76.6% of patients, typically with normal or near-normal coronary arteries.
Type II Kounis syndrome occurs in 22.3% of individuals with quiescent prior coronary disease, triggered by acute myocardial infarction with platelet activation.

5.1% of patients exhibit type III Kounis syndrome, manifesting as stent thrombosis (subtype IIIa) or stent restenosis (subtype IIIb) due to stent polymers, metals, eluted drugs, dual antiplatelet therapy, and environmental exposures.

Contrast media-induced Kounis syndrome can lead to major complications including a 7.7% mortality rate and a 23.1% cardiac arrest rate, with some deaths from multiple organ failure and recurrent cardiac arrest.
Treatment with glucocorticoids plus H1 (cetirizine, loratadine) and H2 (cimetidine, famotidine) receptor blockers can completely resolve symptoms of type I Kounis syndrome.
Beta-blockers should be avoided in Kounis syndrome management because they can exacerbate coronary artery spasm.
Mast cell degranulation occurs when relevant antigens bridge 2,000 adjacent surface-bound antibodies to create the critical 1,000 antibody bridges required for activation.

Gadoteric acid showed dose-dependent cytotoxicity and moderate genotoxicity at high concentrations in NIH3T3 fibroblasts, suggesting DNA damage results from cytotoxic rather than direct genotoxic mechanisms.
An etiopathogenetic relationship has been shown between Kounis syndrome type I and COVID-19, mediated by cytokine storm.

Sodium metabisulfite, a preservative found in all commercially available adrenaline formulations, has been linked to cases of anaphylactic shock during epidural anesthesia for caesarean sections, complicating anaphylaxis treatment in sulfite-sensitive patients.
Nitrates and calcium channel blockers can prevent allergic coronary artery spasm in Kounis syndrome.
Glucagon has been successfully used as an alternative to adrenaline to treat anaphylaxis in patients on beta-blockers.
Acute allergic reactions caused by contrast media, acting as a rapid and intense physical stressor, may trigger Takotsubo syndrome.

Il13ra1 knockout mice were resistant to dopaminergic neuron death from chronic peripheral LPS administration, suggesting the IL-13/IL13RA1 pathway increases susceptibility of dopaminergic neurons to inflammatory/oxidative damage rather than directly causing PD pathology.
Histamine receptor expression is altered in Parkinson's disease patients, implicating histamine signaling in PD pathogenesis.
Elevated histamine levels were observed in the substantia nigra and putamen of Parkinson's disease patients.
Histamine promotes microglial activation and reactive oxygen species formation via H1R and H4R stimulation, while H4R receptor inhibition showed a protective effect in PD experimental models.

Population-level studies found that people diagnosed with asthma, allergic rhinitis, or atopic dermatitis had higher rates of dementia and Alzheimer's disease than people without these allergic conditions.
IgE-mediated allergic disorders were found to be more common among Alzheimer's disease patients than non-sufferers.
AD incidence was elevated among people with allergic rhinitis under high particulate matter exposure conditions.
Administration of IL-4 or IL-13 decreased amyloid-beta accumulation and improved cognitive performance in some Alzheimer's disease models.
Increased IL-4 production in the hippocampus was shown to cause an increase in amyloid-beta formation, contradicting other AD model findings of IL-4's beneficial effect.
Histamine and diamine oxidase levels were lower in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis patients compared to healthy controls.
A mast-cell-associated protease, tryptase, was significantly elevated in the cerebrospinal fluid of multiple sclerosis patients, while histamine and methylhistamine were not.
Histamine acting on H1 and H2 receptors was shown to play a detrimental role in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), an animal model of MS.
Strategies targeting IL-4 could mitigate EAE progression in certain models, though this reflects immunomodulation rather than a causative Type 2 role in MS.
Histamine was shown to protect motor neurons in ALS models through activation of the AKT and ERK1/2 pathways and by increasing mitochondrial function and ATP production.
Human ALS studies have shown alterations in T-cell-related cytokine responses, including IL-13-related pathways.

Binding studies show histamine H3 receptors in the brains of dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) patients are not altered by disease overall, but correlate with the presence of psychosis and hallucinations.
IL-4 is upregulated in peripheral blood during early stages of Lewy body disease (e.g., mild cognitive impairment with Lewy bodies) but does not differentiate full DLB from healthy controls.
Low IL-4 levels correlated with faster disease progression in longitudinal analyses of dementia with Lewy bodies.
IL-13 findings in DLB are conflicting: one study found no significant cytokine changes, while another found elevated IL-13 associated with IL-10, IL-1α, and amyloid-β pathology in DLB brain tissue.
Elevated peripheral blood levels of IL-4 and allergy-related chemokines (eotaxin and eotaxin-3) were found in Huntington's disease, with some parameters associated with disease progression.
In Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (a human prion disease), cerebrospinal fluid IL-4 and IL-10 levels were substantially elevated compared to controls, suggesting compensatory Th2-related CNS signals.
In murine prion infection models, loss of IL-10 accelerated disease onset and progression, indicating a protective role for IL-10, whereas loss of IL-4 or IL-13 alone did not accelerate disease.
IL-13 expression was transiently upregulated early in prion infection in certain contexts, such as in CD14-deficient mice, suggesting time- and context-dependent Type 2 responses.

Postmortem biochemical studies demonstrated increased histamine concentrations in Parkinson's disease but not in multiple system atrophy, indicating disease-specific differences in histaminergic pathway involvement among parkinsonian disorders.
Elevated peripheral blood levels of IL-4 and allergy-related chemokines eotaxin and eotaxin-3 have been reported in Huntington's disease, with some parameters associated with disease progression.

Immune dysregulation in Huntington's disease involves the innate immune system and myeloid cells, with increased cytokine release from HD myeloid cells and enhanced microglial responsiveness to inflammation.

In Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows substantially elevated levels of IL-4 and IL-10 compared to controls, suggesting compensatory Th2-related signaling in the CNS during prion disease.
In murine models of prion infection, loss of IL-10 results in accelerated disease onset and progression, suggesting IL-10 has a protective or disease-modifying effect.

Unlike IL-10, loss of IL-4 or IL-13 alone in murine prion infection models does not accelerate disease, indicating these Type 2 cytokines are not functionally equivalent to IL-10 despite shared anti-inflammatory classification.

IL-13 expression can be transiently upregulated early in prion infection in certain contexts, such as in CD14-deficient mice, suggesting time- and context-dependent Type 2 cytokine responses rather than sustained involvement throughout disease.
Postmortem research in progressive supranuclear palsy shows cytokine expression and microglial activation indicating neuroinflammation, but does not show presence of characteristic Th2 cytokines.

Postmortem biochemical studies show increased histamine concentrations in Parkinson's disease but not in multiple system atrophy, indicating disease-specific differences in histaminergic pathway involvement among parkinsonian disorders.
Glehnia littoralis extract dose-dependently inhibited degranulation in RBL-2H3 mast cells.
GL treatment markedly reduced airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and granulocyte infiltration in OVA-induced asthmatic mice.
GL treatment lowered serum OVA-specific IgE levels in the asthma mouse model.
GL treatment partially restored TGF-β1 levels that had been altered by allergic airway inflammation.
Imperatorin was identified as the primary bioactive constituent of GL suppressing FcεRI- and TLR-mediated NF-κB/AP-1 and IRF signaling while reducing MAPK phosphorylation.
Transcriptomic profiling showed imperatorin reversed 186 antigen-induced genes enriched in FcεRI and inflammatory pathways in mast cells.
GL and imperatorin attenuated TNF-α and IL-6 production in house dust mite-stimulated human PBMCs, supporting translational relevance.
In patients with persistent unexplained dyspnea after acute pulmonary embolism, peak oxygen consumption on invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing was reduced to a mean of 71.0% of predicted.
The cardiovascular exercise limit in these post-PE dyspnea patients was explained by preload failure, evidenced by a low right atrial pressure at peak exercise.
There was no evidence of ventilatory inefficiency in this cohort, with a normal VE/VCO2 slope.
Dead space ventilation at peak exercise was increased in the post-PE dyspnea cohort.
Among post-PE patients referred for skin biopsy, the large majority (9 of 11, 82%) had confirmed small fiber neuropathy.
The authors hypothesize a mechanistic link between an inflammatory PE insult, peripheral neuronal injury, and resultant preload failure driving dyspnea.
Salivary anti-Nucleocapsid secretory IgA (sIgA) levels were significantly higher in post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients than in COVID-recovered individuals.
Serum complement C3 concentrations were statistically significantly decreased in PCS patients compared with COVID-recovered individuals, suggesting complement consumption.
Serum C4 levels were lower in PCS than in COVID-recovered individuals but the difference did not reach statistical significance.
Serum Factor B, Factor H, and total hemolytic complement activity (CH50) were similar between PCS and COVID-recovered cohorts.

A combined logistic regression model using salivary anti-N sIgA and serum C3 discriminated PCS patients from COVID-recovered controls with excellent performance (AUC=0.93), outperforming either marker alone.
No statistically significant correlation was found between salivary anti-N sIgA and previously measured serum anti-N IgG in the same cohort.
Patients experiencing fatigue exhibited greater C3 consumption in both PCS and COVID-recovered cohorts, though additional factors likely contribute since not all comparisons reached significance.
No association was found between C3 levels and other frequently reported PCS symptoms (headache, muscle pain, cough, anosmia, joint pain).

No difference in circulating immune complex levels was found between PCS and COVID-recovered cohorts, with only 1 positive individual in COVID-recovered and 3 in PCS, suggesting immune complex formation is not a general pathogenic mechanism in PCS.
C3 remained lower in PCS than COVID-recovered when stratified by vaccine doses, reaching statistical significance only in non-reinfected individuals who received three vaccine doses.
In PCS patients infected before vaccination, salivary anti-N sIgA showed a trend toward increase following recent reinfection, though not statistically significant.

A significant negative correlation was found between serum anti-N IgG and CH50 hemolytic activity in PCS patients with two vaccine doses and a recent reinfection, suggesting higher anti-N IgG is associated with greater complement consumption.
A negative correlation was found between serum anti-N IgG and Factor H in PCS patients with three vaccine doses, potentially reflecting FH binding to the Nucleocapsid.
No significant correlation was found between serum anti-full-length Spike IgG (or subclasses IgG1/2/4) or anti-RBD IgG subclasses and CH50, in contrast to the anti-N IgG/CH50 correlation.
The TGFBR1 p.Asp400Gly variant showed decreased protein expression compared with wild-type in functional analysis.
Both TGFBR1 variants (p.Asp400Gly and p.Leu196Pro) identified in the two LDS patients showed reduced TGF-beta signaling activity, suggesting a loss-of-function effect.
Two patients with Loeys-Dietz syndrome harboring TGFBR1 variants p.Asp400Gly and p.Leu196Pro presented with severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction.
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in the two LDS patients was transient and improved following initiation and optimization of medical heart failure therapy.
Histopathologic analysis of right ventricular biopsy specimens from the affected patients revealed limited interstitial and perivascular fibrosis.

Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from DGAN patients into db/db mice worsened gut dysmotility compared to control transplants.
Butyrate, the predominant metabolite produced by F. prausnitzii, attenuated neuronal apoptosis in enteric neurons cultured under high-glucose conditions.
Butyrate treatment was accompanied by enhanced BCL2 expression in neurons under high-glucose stress, consistent with an anti-apoptotic effect.
Butyrate treatment reduced levels of cleaved (activated) caspase-3 in neurons under high-glucose stress, indicating reduced apoptotic signaling.
Butyrate's neuroprotective effect against high-glucose-induced apoptosis was linked to activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade.
The study proposes existence of a gut microbiota-enteric nervous system (ENS) axis underlying diabetic gastrointestinal autonomic neuropathy (DGAN) pathogenesis.
ME/CFS patients reported significantly greater subjective sensory problems than healthy controls.
The P50 suppression index, an ERP measure of early sensory gating, did not significantly differ between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls on the auditory paired click task.
The ME/CFS group showed a significantly reduced P300 ERP amplitude compared with healthy controls on the auditory oddball task, indicating impaired higher-order information processing.
Global DTI-ALPS index, a measure of glymphatic function, was significantly lower in ME/CFS patients than in healthy controls.
The right hemisphere DTI-ALPS index was significantly lower in ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
