No significant difference in interhemispheric asymmetry of glymphatic function (asymmetry index) was found between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls.
Lower global DTI-ALPS index was associated with greater severity of sleep disturbance in ME/CFS.
Lower global DTI-ALPS index was associated with greater severity of impaired concentration in ME/CFS.
The phase III RituxME trial found that rituximab did not demonstrate efficacy in an unselected population of ME/CFS patients.
A phase II trial of therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) in post-COVID condition failed to demonstrate efficacy in an unselected patient population.
Observational data suggest TPE may benefit patients across these post-infectious syndromes who have a demonstrable autoantibody burden, in contrast to unselected trial populations.
Immune dysregulation involving persistent inflammation, autoantibody production, and cellular immune dysfunction may underlie PTLDS, long COVID, ME/CFS, and PANS/PANDAS.
Prefrontal cortical TGF-β1 levels were significantly elevated in rats subjected to the 10-day sleep deprivation fatigue model compared to controls.
Peripheral (serum) TGF-β1 levels did not differ significantly between fatigue-model rats and controls.
Striatal TGF-β1 levels did not differ significantly between fatigue-model rats and controls, indicating region-specific TGF-β1 upregulation restricted to the prefrontal cortex.
Fatigue-model rats showed markedly reduced spontaneous alternation rates in the Y-maze test compared to controls, indicating impaired spatial working memory/cognitive function.
Fatigue-model rats exhibited significantly increased anxiety-like behavior in the open field test compared to controls.
Daytime short-term locomotor activity in the open field test was unchanged in fatigue-model rats compared to controls.
Dry eye, strabismus, amblyopia, and blue sclera were among several ophthalmic conditions found to be more common in EDS respondents than in general population estimates.
High myopia was reported by approximately 40% of EDS respondents, exceeding population estimates of 20-30%, making myopia the most prevalent ophthalmic condition in the cohort.

Glaucoma, posterior vitreous detachment, and retinal tear/detachment presented at younger ages than typically expected in EDS respondents, conditions that could cause significant morbidity if undetected.
Ophthalmic surgeries in EDS patients were generally well tolerated, though persistent postoperative pain was frequently reported.

Conservative multidisciplinary management with rehabilitation led to gradual neurological improvement and radiological stability in this EDS patient with ICH.
Patients with EDS had an approximately 11-fold higher proportion of recorded CRPS diagnoses compared to patients without EDS in a large US claims database.
Among EDS patients, those with co-occurring CRPS were more predominantly female (96.7%) than EDS patients without CRPS (81.3%).
Among CRPS cases co-occurring with EDS, the majority (76.8%) were classified as type 1 disease.
Lower-limb involvement was the most frequent anatomical presentation among CRPS cases co-occurring with EDS, occurring in 49.0% of cases.
Ankle taping acutely improved static balance (single-leg stance) in dancers with chronic ankle instability classified as non-structural (functional CAI or non-hypermobile).
Ankle taping did not significantly improve static balance in dancers with structural instability, defined as mechanical CAI or generalized ligamentous hypermobility.
Across all dancers, ankle taping produced no significant improvements in dynamic balance (Y balance, side hop, figure-of-8) or other functional test outcomes.
Among 85 dancers completing the study, 74.1% reported at least one prior ankle sprain and 64.7% met criteria for chronic ankle instability (CAIT ≤24).
Mean condyle-C1 interval (CCI) was slightly but significantly larger in Chiari malformation type I patients compared to controls.
C1 socket depth-to-length ratio, condyle depth-to-depth ratio, and atlas tilt angle did not differ significantly between CMI patients and controls.
Within CMI patients, CCI showed a modest positive correlation with joint hypermobility.
AOJ-related morphometric measures showed moderate correlations with several established craniocervical and posterior fossa morphometrics in CMI patients.
Among generalized joint hypermobility studies, a Beighton Scoring System (BSS) threshold of ≥4 was the most commonly used cutoff, followed by ≥5.
Among joint-specific or arthroscopy joint hypermobility studies, a BSS threshold of ≥4 was also the most common cutoff, followed by ≥5 and use of the full BSS scale.
Joint-specific or arthroscopy joint hypermobility studies were published significantly more recently than generalized joint hypermobility studies.
Generalized joint hypermobility studies more frequently reported separate subject sex and age data compared to joint-specific or arthroscopy studies, which more often combined this information.
Generalized joint hypermobility studies were predominantly Evidence Level II, whereas joint-specific or arthroscopy studies were predominantly Evidence Level III.
Generalized joint hypermobility studies used prospective research designs more often than joint-specific or arthroscopy joint hypermobility studies.
Across all 64 included studies, BSS scores were reported to influence most/all study outcomes in over half of studies, and some outcomes in over a quarter of studies.
Most of the 64 included studies reported that Beighton Scoring System scores influenced most or all study outcomes, with a smaller proportion reporting partial influence.
Overall study quality and risk of bias were comparable between generalized joint hypermobility studies and joint-specific or arthroscopy joint hypermobility studies.

The authors describe a surgical technique for intracapsular closure of both anterolateral and modified midanterior periportal capsulotomies during hip arthroscopy, intended for patients at higher risk of postoperative hip instability such as those with borderline dysplasia or joint hypermobility.

A novel frameshift duplication variant c.980_984dup (p.Ile329Alafs*72) in COL1A2 was identified by exome sequencing and attributed as the cause of hereditary obstructive sleep apnea syndrome in the patient.
Treatment of the patient's OSAS with nocturnal active positive airway pressure (APAP) led to symptomatic improvement.

Clinical assessment of suspected hip dysplasia should include evaluation of generalized joint hypermobility, hip range of motion, symptom-reproducing tests, and extra-articular structures.
Evidence supporting non-surgical management of hip dysplasia, such as exercise and patient education, is emerging but remains limited.
Camouflaging scores significantly predicted central sensitivity syndrome (CSS) symptom severity across the sample.
Autistic people with a CSS had higher camouflaging scores (mean 130.28) than other diagnostic groups, significantly higher than the comparison group.
Both autism-only and CSS-only groups had significantly higher camouflaging scores than the comparison group, but did not differ significantly from each other (119.35 vs. 107.94).
Among people with a CSS, autistic individuals reported a significantly more negative effect of chronic illness on their life than nonautistic individuals.
Among people with a CSS, the number of symptoms experienced did not differ significantly between autistic and nonautistic people, despite autistic people reporting greater life impact.
Unsupervised hierarchical clustering of patient-reported symptoms failed to identify distinct patient subgroups, indicating highly heterogeneous symptom presentation among suspected MCAS patients.
Nearly half of surveyed patients (43%) reported signs and symptoms aligning with the first diagnostic criterion for MCAS.

The authors propose that CSU chronification begins with FcεRI/BTK-dependent mast cell degranulation as the initiating stage.
Eosinophil tissue-factor activation is proposed to drive a coagulation-complement loop as the second stage of CSU chronification.
FXIIIa-positive dendrocytes are proposed to phagocytose and prime T cells via OX40/OX40L signaling as the third stage of chronification.
Th2-driven M2 macrophage polarization coupled with autoantibody-mediated mast cell reactivation is proposed as the fourth stage sustaining CSU chronicity.
JAK/STAT and IFN-λ1 signaling are proposed as the fifth stage that sustains a chronic dermal immune niche in CSU.
Transcriptomic hub gene analysis and cytokine profiling are cited as further support for the proposed five-stage chronification model.
The authors propose targeting upstream checkpoints including BTK, JAK, and OX40/OX40L as therapeutic strategies for sustained control of treatment-refractory CSU.

Autonomic nervous system function appears altered in individuals with ASD compared to their first-degree relative controls, consistent with prior literature suggesting ANS dysfunction in ASD.
The study explores the relationship between gut microbiome composition and autonomic indices (the gut-brain axis) in individuals with ASD, a link not previously examined.

The gut-brain-axis (combined autonomic and microbiome markers) is examined for correlation with clinical presentation of ASD, including comorbidities such as anxiety, cardiovascular issues, and gastrointestinal dysfunction.

Combined gut-brain-axis biomarkers (autonomic and microbiome indices) are proposed to have predictive capability for subtyping ASD cases and could assist in ASD screening and diagnosis beyond current subjective psychological testing.

A novel X-linked missense variant in APOO (MIC26), c.350T>C (p.I117T), was identified in a family with variable mitochondrial disease presentations including autistic features, cognitive impairment, and lactic acidosis.
The variant follows an X-linked recessive inheritance pattern, with the mother heterozygous and proband hemizygous, and phenotype in female carriers depending on X-chromosome inactivation skewing.

The proband presented with progressive developmental delay, irritability, fatigue, hypotonia, weight loss, gastrointestinal and body temperature dysautonomia, repetitive infections, cognitive impairment and autistic behaviour, initially suspected as autism spectrum disorder due to speech regression and hand stereotypies.
Blood tests showed consistently elevated lactate and pyruvate, severe metabolic acidosis, and an altered carnitine profile in the proband.

Treatment with L-carnitine, biotin and CoQ10 was associated with normalisation of brain MRI, weight gain, decreased fatigue and irritability, and improvement of autistic behaviour in the proband, with the mother also responding well to L-carnitine and CoQ10.
Patient-derived fibroblasts showed reduced steady-state levels and slower electrophoretic mobility of the mitochondrial 22 kDa MIC26 form compared to controls.

In organello import assays showed the mutant MIC26_I117T undergoes altered two-step processing, producing intermediate and mature forms with slower electrophoretic mobility (apparent sizes 20.6 vs 19.1 kDa and 18.5 vs 17.8 kDa) compared to wild-type.
MIC26I117T showed weaker binding to the inner mitochondrial membrane, being more easily released by carbonate extraction than wild-type MIC26.
In patient fibroblasts, MIC60 was found mainly incorporated into the MIB complex rather than the MICOS complex, and this altered distribution was rescued by expression of wild-type MIC26.
TEM analysis of patient fibroblasts revealed wider and fewer cristae and fewer cristae junctions per cristae compared to controls and MIC26-WT rescued cells.
Oxygen consumption rates were reduced in patient fibroblasts grown in galactose media but not glucose media, compared with controls.
In yeast, the Δmic26 null strain showed impaired colony growth under ethanol stress, and this growth defect was not rescued by expression of the mutant I127T allele, confirming pathogenicity.

Drosophila dApoO knockout flies displayed age-related neuromotor dysfunction with reduced climbing indexes (53-70% of control at 2 days, 21-36% at 10 days) and significantly shortened lifespan (median survival 39% in males and 44% in females of control).

dApoO knockout flies showed severely decreased CI-linked and CII-linked mitochondrial respiration, reduced steady-state OXPHOS complex I-V levels, and reduced enzymatic activities, along with abnormal cristae junctions and wider cristae in brain and muscle.

Unlike MICOS13 (QIL1) null variants which cause severe autosomal recessive encephalopathy and hepatopathy (COXPD37) with combined respiratory chain enzymatic deficiencies, the APOO missense variant produced a milder phenotype without respiratory chain enzymatic deficiency in patient fibroblasts, likely because MIC26 is a peripheral MICOS component and its paralog MIC27 remains present.
Children with ADHD showed lower evening and overall diurnal salivary alpha-amylase levels compared with typically developing children, after adjusting for age.
Children with autism spectrum disorder showed lower diurnal salivary alpha-amylase secretion compared with typically developing children, adjusted for age.
The percentage change in salivary cortisol and alpha-amylase following an academic performance test and a moral cognition task did not differ between ADHD, ASD, SLD, and TD groups.

Overall hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis functioning, indexed by salivary cortisol, did not differ between the clinical (ADHD, ASD, SLD) and comparison (TD) groups, in contrast to alterations found in autonomic (alpha-amylase) diurnal functioning.
Bumetanide was not superior to placebo on the primary outcome, change in SRS-2 total score at day 91.
Bumetanide produced a significant reduction in repetitive behavior symptoms compared to placebo, as measured by the Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised.
Bumetanide showed no significant effect on sensory processing symptoms compared to placebo, as measured by the Sensory Profile.
Bumetanide showed no significant effect on irritability compared to placebo, as measured by the Aberrant Behavior Checklist Irritability Subscale.
Orthostatic hypotension occurred significantly more often in the bumetanide group than in the placebo group.
Hypokalemia occurred significantly more often in the bumetanide group than in the placebo group.
No significant wash-out effect was observed after discontinuation of bumetanide following the 28-day wash-out period.
The occurrence of diuretic-related adverse effects (orthostatic hypotension, hypokalemia) did not statistically influence the treatment outcome of bumetanide in this trial.
In a galvanic skin response study, autistic young adults showed reduced habituation of autonomic responses to a repeated metronomic auditory sequence compared to age-matched neurotypical controls.
In an independent MEG study spanning pre-adolescents to young adults, autistic participants exhibited reduced habituation of auditory neural responses compared to non-autistic participants.
Prior literature reviewed indicates autistic individuals do not systematically differ from controls in basic sensory acuity or sensitivity, in contrast to habituation deficits.

Poorer performance on select individual items and cluster scales of the neonatal NBAS at ~2 weeks old was associated with increased ASD-associated maladaptive behaviours in adolescence, with the strongest associations seen for neonatal self-regulation, response to auditory input, and autonomic nervous system regulation.

Infants scoring in the lowest tertile (poorest performance) on the NBAS Regulation of State cluster had adolescent BASC-2 TRS Developmental Social Disorders T-scores 2.9 points higher than infants in the higher two tertiles, indicating more ASD-associated behaviours, in covariate-adjusted models.

Three patients from two unrelated families with an atypical distal 7q11.23 deletion that excludes the ELN gene nonetheless present with distinctive Williams-Beuren syndrome craniofacial features and neurocognitive profile.
The study supports a critical role for the CLIP2, GTF2IRD1, and GTF2I genes within the atypical deletion region in producing the WBS neurobehavioral profile and craniofacial features.
The findings highlight a possible role of the HIP1 gene, located within the atypical deletion, in autism spectrum disorder.

A subgroup of WBS individuals with the atypical distal ELN-excluding deletion is delineated as not being associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular defects, in contrast to typical WBS deletions that include ELN.
Meta-analysis found that individuals with autism spectrum disorder show a longer latency of the pupil response compared to non-ASD individuals, representing a substantial group difference.
Evidence regarding baseline pupil size and amplitude of pupillary change in ASD versus non-ASD individuals was conflicting across included studies.
Children with ASD showed reduced resting-state heart rate variability compared to neurotypical children.
The reduction in HRV in children with ASD compared to neurotypical children was greater among those taking psychotropic medication.
More severe repetitive behaviors, as measured by the ADOS-2, were associated with decreased resting HRV in children with ASD.

In a bilateral cavernous nerve injury rat model, early sustained sympathetic hyperactivity and parasympathetic suppression in the corpus cavernosum were detected and correlated significantly with fibrotic progression.

Electroacupuncture at Zusanli (ST36) reversed the cavernous autonomic imbalance, significantly improved erectile function recovery, and attenuated penile pathological remodeling in the BCNI rat model.
Proteomic analysis showed that ST36 electroacupuncture markedly upregulated cavernous L-arginine biosynthesis, with the key enzyme ASS1 enriched in cavernous endothelial cells.

Pharmacological inhibition of the L-arginine pathway with alpha-Methyl-DL-aspartate abolished EA's protective effects on erectile function, and this effect was rescued by arginine supplementation, confirming that EA acts via L-arginine/nitric oxide signaling.
Most patients with Somatic Symptom Disorder met criteria for the multi-system subcategory of the functional somatic disorder (FSD) classification.

Patients classified with multi-system FSD showed greater psychological and behavioural burden, including higher somatosensory amplification, perceived stress, health anxiety, and negative affect, than other FSD subgroups.
Single-system FSD classification showed limited correspondence with established syndrome-based diagnoses such as fibromyalgia or irritable bowel syndrome.
Comorbid musculoskeletal, vascular, and neurological conditions were common among SSD patients but were often not aligned with the patient's presenting symptom system.

Amiodarone reduced superoxide dismutase (SOD) antioxidant enzyme activity in lung tissue.

Amiodarone increased interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels as part of the inflammatory response.
Amiodarone activated the profibrotic cascade by increasing TGF-beta1 levels in rat lung tissue, which was reduced by naringenin co-treatment.

Naringenin co-treatment significantly attenuated histopathological changes and reduced fibrosis scores compared to the amiodarone-only group, indicating a protective effect against drug-induced pulmonary fibrosis.

Experimentally induced hyperuricemia significantly reduced LISW-induced visceral hypersensitivity in a rat model of IBS.
LISW-induced head shock waves increased ileal mucosal permeability as measured by the Evans blue method, and this was ameliorated by hyperuricemia.
LISW increased rectal CRFR1 mRNA expression, a change that was ameliorated by hyperuricemia treatment.
LISW reduced IL-10 expression in the ileum, and this was restored by hyperuricemia treatment.
Hyperuricemia was associated with reduced IL-1beta expression in the medial prefrontal cortex of LISW-treated animals.
Hyperuricemia was associated with reduced IL-1alpha and IL-1beta expression in the paraventricular nucleus of LISW-treated animals.

The ameliorative effect of hyperuricemia on visceral hypersensitivity was abolished by subdiaphragmatic vagotomy or atropine treatment, indicating dependence on vagal cholinergic brain-gut communication.

Rome V replaces the term 'functional' with 'disorders of gut-brain interaction' (DGBI) to reframe these conditions as positive diagnoses rooted in altered gut-brain regulation rather than implying psychological or less-real symptoms.

Rome V refines esophageal disorder criteria by excluding gastroesophageal reflux disease and major motor disorders, aligning with the Lyon Consensus 2.0 and Chicago Classification v4.0, and by refining globus and functional chest pain definitions to avoid unnecessary interventions.

Rome V improves phenotyping of functional dyspepsia by meal-related symptoms and clarifies distinctions from chronic nausea and vomiting syndrome, gastroparesis, cyclic vomiting syndrome, cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome, rumination, and inability to belch.
Rome V reintroduces abdominal discomfort into IBS diagnostic criteria and changes the symptom frequency threshold used to diagnose IBS.
Rome V renames functional constipation as chronic constipation and redefines abdominal bloating/distension within bowel disorder criteria.

Rome V's anorectal section operationalizes fecal incontinence, defines dyssynergic defecation using objective testing, and formally recognizes rectal hypo- and hypersensitivity, which may guide biofeedback therapy.
A homozygous pathogenic TNXB variant (c.3763dup) was identified in three siblings with classical-like Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (clEDS).

The oldest brother, who met clinical criteria for hypermobile EDS (hEDS), was heterozygous for the same TNXB variant, similar to the asymptomatic parents, suggesting a possible link between TNXB haploinsufficiency and hEDS.
TNXB expression was significantly lower in homozygous carriers of the c.3763dup variant compared to heterozygous carriers.
No significant difference in TNXB expression was observed between symptomatic (hEDS) and asymptomatic heterozygous carriers of the variant.

IBS is characterized by central sensitization, impaired descending pain inhibition, increased temporal summation, and autonomic dysregulation, producing widespread hyperalgesia that overlaps with pain mechanisms seen in spine surgery patients.
Epidemiologic literature indicates that patients with IBS undergo musculoskeletal and spinal procedures at disproportionately high rates compared to the general population.

Factors associated with IBS have been linked to greater postoperative pain, elevated opioid requirements, slower functional recovery, and reduced satisfaction after spine surgery, though direct IBS-specific spine surgery data remain limited.
IBS may confound preoperative spine assessment by mimicking radicular, discogenic, or sacroiliac pain patterns.
